429:
- Cook, or something?
- That all depends on ability.
430:
I know one guy, also a “scientist,”
he’s got three grades of schooling,
431:
and he can draw you a ten-ruble note in half an hour—
you can’t tell it from a real one!
432:
- Well, him?
- Hell knows... I’ll check.
433:
- Sorry, do you have a match?
- I don’t smoke.
434:
- What? - No, not him.
- A cop. - Exactly.
435:
The check showed that at the addresses
of Docent’s accomplices, the helmet isn’t there.
436:
The last version remains—the cloakroom attendant
Prokhorov.
437:
However, it wasn’t possible to check this version:
Prokhorov didn’t show up for the meeting.
438:
He likely suspected something. He quit his job,
didn’t show up at home.
440:
And to you—our deepest apologies, enormous thanks.
Take off the wig, wash off the tattoos,
441:
go home, celebrate New Year’s. Thank you very much.
- And mine?
442: And we’ll return your wards to their place today.
443:
And if the cloakroom attendant turns up,
we might be needed again?
444:
I didn’t want to tell you, but today Bely—the Docent—
escaped from the colony.
445:
Unbelievable, but true. It’s dangerous for you
to stay in that appearance.
446:
Maybe tomorrow? It’s New Year’s after all,
and in their own way they tried too.
447:
We live outside the city; it’s unlikely
Docent can find us.
448:
All right, but not a step off the dacha!
Yes, we forwarded your letter
449:
to Sheremetyev’s wife—here’s her reply.
Addressed to him.
450:
- You’ll have lunch with us on the first, promise?
- We promise!
451:
Pity—such a good woman, and her father’s
a fence, a speculator.
452:
Why are you yelling? Who allowed you to come out?
- He’s here... A bad person.
454:
The New Year has come. I wish that in this
new year everything will be new for you.
455:
Anything can happen, but know this:
Wherever you are, wherever I am,
456:
I will always remember you,
I will definitely find you.
457:
- And now... one minute...
- Where’d he go?
458:
Who knows? You can’t understand anything
about him now.
459:
What’s to understand? He says he’ll find us anywhere
and slit our throats.
461:
They say he took Ryaboy with a razor across the throat—snip, and goodbye.
- Totally gone rabid, the jackal.
462:
Who has come to you? Santa Claus has come to you,
he brought you gifts!
463:
- Fedya, come here. - What did I do?
- Come on, come on. Wear them in good health—house slippers.
464:
- What the hell do I need them for? I don’t even have a home.
- You will—everything’s ahead.
465:
- And for now they’ll come in handy in prison. Wear them.
- All you know is to croak.
466:
This is for you, Vasya... Gavrila Petrovich, this is for you.
- Thank you.
467:
- Pure wool.
- This is for you too.
470:
- What, do you have to get drunk like a pig?
- What else is there to do?
471:
We could just sit and talk
heart to heart.
472:
I’m not a prosecutor to talk heart to heart with you.
- We could play a game.
473:
Look at him go! Found a sucker to play with you!
You’ve got nine aces in the deck.
474: Why does it have to be cards?
475:
Here’s a good game—cities.
I say “Moscow,”
476:
and you on the last letter “A”—“Astrakhan.”
And you on “N”—“Novgorod,” get it?
478:
Vorkuta.
Why? I did time there.
479:
- Okay. And you, then, on “A.”
- Jambul. - What does Jambul have to do with it?
480:
Because it’s warm there, that’s my home,
that’s my mom.
481:
Then let’s play this way. I’ll go out, you’ll
hide something, I’ll come back—I’ll find it.
482:
- You’d better find our helmet.
- Shut up.
483:
- We hide it, and he’ll peek through the crack?
- Why? You go out and hide it.
484:
And you watch so I don’t peek.
Why me? Anything happens—right away Fedya.
485:
- I’ll rip your mouth open, you filthy little bastard!
- Mouth, mouth...
486:
- Docent, were you ever little?
- I was.
487:
- Did you have a mom and dad?
- I did.
488: Why are you so mean? Why like a dog?
490:
- Came on your own.
- Ah, you’re here too.
491:
I was about to drop by you, but I can feel
there’s an ambush there.
492: Mityai, I need to lie low.
494:
- Where are we going?
- Come on.
495:
- Sorry, doctor, for bothering you for nothing.
- It’s fine.
496:
Give him some valerian, warm tea, and let him sleep.
- Thank you.
497:
- Does it hurt, Garik?
- It hurts, Vasya. Read.
499:
“Hello, dear Daddy! We found out that
you’re in prison
500:
and we were very happy, because we thought
you had died.”
501:
What bastard tattled to that little punk
about Hmyr?
502:
“And Mom was happy too, because
when the letter came she cried
503:
all day, and before that she said
you were a test pilot.”
504: A test pilot—more like a raid pilot...
505:
“And I’m glad anyway that you’re alive, because
Mom says
507:
Exactly! Weak-willed—swiped the common money
and blamed it on the taxi driver.
508: Beat it! I’ll smash your horns, radish!
510:
Aren’t you ashamed! You’re 40 years old,
half your life is already gone.
511:
What’s behind you? What’s in the present?
What’s ahead?
512:
Darkness, filth, and nothing human!
Come to your senses before it’s too late. That’s my advice.
513:
Hear me, Docent, we need to bail:
That doctor lady will snitch to the cops.
514:
- She won’t. - Why?
- I did her with a razor across the throat...
515: she’s lying in the well—go take a look.
516: How much did I have? One year.
518:
How much for the kindergarten and the apartment?
Let it be ten!
520: And for a lousy 14 years I’m supposed to put up with this viper?
521:
The one who put an old woman in a well?
Do what you want, but I’m going to the police.
523:
And you? You’ll keep tolerating him
till you die, yes?
524:
Vas, I told him earlier: I’ve got a runny nose,
and he...
525:
Enough, I’m sick of your runny nose.
Come here...
527:
- What are you doing?
- We’re going to beat the carpet.
528:
Here’s the thing, comrades. Finita la commedia.
First of all, I’m taking this off.
530:
I’ll do my time and that’s it. I’ll quit!
Get a job.
531:
- As what? A watchman at your native collective farm.
- Why a watchman?
532:
I can shovel snow, lay bricks, or work
as a translator—I know English.
533:
If only we’d brought the hat too!
Who’s Docent? A crook.
534:
- There are lots of crooks, but only one hat.
- If we turned in the helmet, they’d cut our time.
535: Where did he put it? We’ve checked everything.
536:
Crook! Did I tell you I have a runny nose?
And you: “Mouth, mouth.”
537:
- Made me dive in that freezing cold!
- When did he make you dive?
538:
When they nabbed us. Remember, he says,
“I’m fishing,” and you dive.
539:
- Wait, what did he say about fishing then?
- “I was fishing in an ice hole,
540:
and you,” he says, “Squinty, can you swim?”
- He hid the helmet in the ice hole—that’s it!
541:
Exactly! I remember, bad person!
In an ice hole—in Malakhovka!
542:
Why didn’t you say so? You pig! At least leave a note when you hang yourself.
- Let’s go.
543:
- And him?
- Nothing, let them pick him up themselves. Carrying a hog like that. Let’s go!
545:
- There’s nothing there.
- It’s there, on the bottom. We need to dive.
546:
Why me? Anything happens—right away Squinty.
Vas, tell him to go in himself.
547: I can’t! It’s cold, I’ll get sick.
548:
- Just tried to hang himself, and now he’s afraid of catching cold!
- Physical culture greetings!
550:
- Where’s the boat station?
- Over there.
551: I’d finish you off, but I haven’t got time to mess around!
552:
Now it’s two pieces.
And there at the dacha—one more.
554:
- One!
- Well done, Fyodor Petrovich, well done!
555:
- Two.
- The more we turn in, the better.
